newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Tula refinery expansion to improve gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Tula refinery expansion to improve gasoline.

text.p: The just completed expansion at Mexico's Tula refinery aim to boost gasoline output and quality, state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) director general Adrian Lajous said on Monday.
The projects' construction cost a total $696 million, he added at the official start-up of the plants on Monday.
"The first of these units will improves the quality of fuel oil and converts a part of the volume to value-added products," Lajous said.
The main addition is a hydrodesulphurization plant with the capacity to produce 42,000 barrels per day (bpd) of low-sulfur fuel oil and a smaller quantity of diesel and gasoline, Pemex said.

Also built were an alkylation plant with output capacity of pf 7,677 bpd of alkylates, which improve the quality of gasolines. A pentane and hexane isomerization plant will have the capacity to produce 15,000 bpd, also to produce high-quality gasolines, Pemex said.

With the completion of the projects, Mexico ended an ecological program of energy projects financed by the Japanese government through the Ex-Im bank and the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund, Lajous said.
"This far-reaching program transformed the national system of refining, allowing it to comply with environmental norms adopted by the Mexican government," Lajous said.
New environmental regulations that enter into effect January 1998, have spurred the government to promote the use of natural gas and lead-free gasoline, instead of more contaminating fuels.
